title: The abundance and radial distribution of faint and ultra-faint dwarfs in galaxy clusters
summary: Cosmological simulations of galaxy clusters are unable to resolve dwarf galaxies due to limited numerical resolution which drives the artificial disruption of dark matter substructures. We address these limitations by combining the results of the cosmological hydrodynamical simulation TNG50 in $Λ$CDM with an empirical model of tidal evolution of cluster galaxies calibrated using high-resolution idealized N-body simulations. Applied to the three most massive clusters in TNG50, our model allows us to study the stellar mass and radial distribution of dwarfs well below the formal resolution limit of the parent simulation. We find that, at $z=0$, clusters with virial mass $M_{200} \sim 10^{14}~\mathrm{M_\odot}$ host a vast population of dwarf galaxies within the virial radius, amounting to $2000$-$7000$ systems with $M_* > 100~\mathrm{M_\odot}$. Taken together, these satellites follow a radial distribution that matches the underlying dark matter profile of the host. However, applying a minimum mass or luminosity threshold for detection, as expected in observational studies, tends to exclude the most heavily-stripped objects, which tend to populate the inner regions. Future surveys targeting ultra-faint galaxies in group and cluster environments, such as those made possible by the Euclid, Rubin, or Roman telescopes, will be fundamental to refute or confirm this prediction.

AI.tldr: The paper combines TNG50 cosmological simulations with a tidal evolution model to predict that massive galaxy clusters host thousands of dwarf galaxies (2000-7000 with M* > 100 M⊙) below the simulation's resolution limit, with radial distributions matching dark matter profiles, though observational detection thresholds bias against heavily-stripped inner dwarfs.
AI.motivation: Cosmological simulations cannot resolve dwarf galaxies in clusters due to limited numerical resolution causing artificial disruption of dark matter substructures.
AI.method: Combined TNG50 ΛCDM hydrodynamical simulation with an empirical tidal evolution model calibrated via high-resolution idealized N-body simulations.
AI.result: At z=0, clusters with M200 ~ 10^14 M⊙ host 2000-7000 dwarf galaxies with M* > 100 M⊙ within the virial radius, following the host's dark matter profile; detection thresholds bias against heavily-stripped inner dwarfs.
AI.conclusion: Future surveys (Euclid, Rubin, Roman) targeting ultra-faint galaxies in clusters can test this prediction.

title: Cluster-green galaxy correlations: where do these galaxies live?
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Green valley (GV) galaxies are thought to represent a transitional population between star-forming and quiescent systems. However, their spatial distribution relative to galaxy systems remains unclear, particularly in relation to the large-scale environmental influence on galaxy quenching. We aim to determine whether GV galaxies preferentially inhabit specific environments within galaxy systems. We analyse the spatial distribution of GV galaxies using the cluster-galaxy cross-correlation function (CCF), based on the hydrodynamical simulation Illustris TNG300-1 (TNG) and observational data from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS). Galaxy systems with $\log(M_{200}/M_{\odot}) \geq 13.5$ are used as cluster centres, while galaxies classified as blue, green, or red serve as tracers for the correlation analysis. In TNG, GV galaxies show an increasing relative fraction with cluster-centric distance, peaking in the outskirts, particularly for low-mass galaxies and haloes, and in some cases the GV fraction exceeds that of red galaxies. SDSS data reveal qualitatively similar trends, with the GV fraction remaining below that of red galaxies at all scales. Mock catalogues built from TNG and matched to SDSS selection functions reproduce the observational signal, indicating that projection effects drive the differences between datasets. GV galaxies preferentially reside in the outskirts of galaxy systems as satellites bound to the central halo, supporting a scenario in which they are transitioning objects influenced by environmental quenching.

AI.tldr: Using TNG300-1 simulations and SDSS data, this study finds that green valley galaxies preferentially reside in the outskirts of massive galaxy systems, supporting an environmental quenching transition scenario.
AI.motivation: Green valley galaxies are thought to be transitioning between star-forming and quiescent phases, but their spatial distribution within large-scale structures and its link to environmental quenching remain poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors analyze the spatial distribution of GV galaxies via cluster-galaxy cross-correlation functions using the Illustris TNG300-1 simulation (log M200 ≥ 13.5) and SDSS observational data, comparing blue, green, and red galaxy populations across radial scales. Mock catalogs matched to SDSS selection functions are constructed from TNG to assess projection effects.
AI.result: In TNG, the GV fraction increases with cluster-centric distance, peaking in the outskirts, especially for low-mass galaxies/haloes, and can exceed the red galaxy fraction. SDSS shows qualitatively similar trends but GV fractions remain below red galaxy fractions at all scales. Mock catalogs reproduce the observational signal, confirming projection effects as the source of discrepancies.
AI.conclusion: GV galaxies preferentially inhabit the outskirts of massive systems as bound satellites, consistent with a picture where they are galaxies undergoing environmental quenching during a transition from star-forming to quiescent states.

title: Itô tracers: continuous-trajectory Lagrangian particles for Eulerian hydrodynamics
summary: Lagrangian tracer particles have long been used to track the history of individual gas parcels in hydrodynamical codes. Particles advected by the cell-centered velocity carry no representation of underlying numerical diffusion, and thus exhibit systematic bias. The Monte-Carlo (MC) tracer resolves this with discrete probabilistic cell-to-cell, flux-based jumps, at the cost of trajectories that are discontinuous in time. We introduce the Itô tracer, a continuous-time Lagrangian particle with moments matched to the advection, diffusion, and dispersion of the gas. A subgrid-scale variant (SGS-Itô) replaces the numerical diffusion with a Smagorinsky--Lilly turbulent diffusivity, illustrating that the form of the diffusion matters less than its magnitude. We validate these methods with a 1D square-pulse advection test and 3D decaying turbulence at $σ_{\rm rms} = 15\,c_{\rm s}$. We compare the different tracer particle methods using several statistical tests. Itô tracers largely reproduce or improve upon MC tracers statistics across column-density maps, joint density histograms, log-density-ratio PDFs, and density power spectra. In the turbulence test, Itô tracers improve the correlation between tracers and gas over the MC tracers by >3\%, and reduce the width of the log-density ratio PDF by nearly 50\%. Relative to classical tracers, these improvements are $\gtrsim$30\% and 230\%, respectively. Because Itô tracers follow a stochastic differential equation, the method maps onto other continuous-trajectory Lagrangian processes (e.g. dust grains, charged particles, cosmic rays), admits variance-reduction techniques, higher-order integrators, and GPU-friendly implementations -- all of which are unavailable to discrete-jump schemes.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces the Itô tracer, a continuous-time Lagrangian particle method that matches gas advection, diffusion, and dispersion moments, outperforming classical and Monte-Carlo tracers in accuracy (e.g., >3% better correlation in turbulence, 50% narrower log-density PDF) while offering advantages like variance reduction, higher-order integrators, and GPU compatibility.
AI.motivation: Classical Lagrangian tracers suffer from systematic bias due to ignoring numerical diffusion, while Monte-Carlo tracers introduce discontinuous trajectories. The motivation is to develop a continuous-time tracer that accurately captures advection, diffusion, and dispersion without these limitations.
AI.method: The Itô tracer is formulated as a stochastic differential equation (SDE) with moments matched to the gas dynamics. A subgrid-scale variant (SGS-Itô) replaces numerical diffusion with Smagorinsky-Lilly turbulent diffusivity. Validation includes 1D square-pulse advection and 3D decaying turbulence tests, comparing against classical and MC tracers via statistics like column-density maps, joint histograms, PDFs, and power spectra.
AI.result: Itô tracers improve correlation with gas over MC tracers by >3% and reduce log-density-ratio PDF width by ~50% in turbulence tests; relative to classical tracers, improvements are ≥30% and 230%, respectively. The SGS-Itô variant shows that diffusion magnitude matters more than its specific form.
AI.conclusion: Itô tracers provide a superior continuous-time Lagrangian framework that maps naturally onto other stochastic physical processes (dust, charged particles, cosmic rays), enabling variance-reduction techniques, higher-order integrators, and GPU-ready implementations — advantages not available to discrete-jump methods.

title: Diffusion-based Galaxy Simulations for the Roman High Latitude Survey
comment: 15 pages, 8 Figure, accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Future weak lensing analyses with the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will require highly realistic image simulations to control shear systematics at unprecedented precision. A key limitation of existing approaches is their reliance on analytic light-profile models, which cannot fully capture the complex, non-parametric morphologies revealed by high-resolution observations. We present a diffusion-based framework for generating realistic galaxy image simulations tailored to the weak lensing requirements of the Roman High Latitude Survey. We construct Roman-like galaxy images from multi-band JWST/NIRCam observations in the GOODS-S and GOODS-N fields, transforming them into the Roman observing regime through point-spread-function matching, pixel-scale conversion, and interloper masking that preserves correlated noise properties. These data are used to train a denoising diffusion probabilistic model to generate multi-band galaxy postage stamps in the Roman Y, J, and H filters. We validate the generated sample against an independent dataset using a consistent photometric pipeline, comparing key galaxy observables including magnitude, size, ellipticity, peak surface brightness, and three-band colors. The generated galaxies reproduce both the marginal distributions and the covariance structure of these properties, with only modest deviations in low-occupancy regions of parameter space. These results demonstrate that diffusion models provide a scalable and physically motivated alternative to analytic simulations, enabling high-fidelity galaxy populations for Roman weak lensing calibration and, more generally, for survey preparation in upcoming cosmological experiments.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a diffusion-based framework for generating realistic multi-band galaxy image simulations for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, using JWST/NIRCam observations transformed to Roman observing conditions. The diffusion model reproduces key galaxy properties (magnitude, size, ellipticity, peak surface brightness, colors) and their covariance structure, offering a scalable alternative to traditional analytic light-profile simulations for weak lensing calibration.
AI.motivation: Existing galaxy image simulations rely on analytic light-profile models that cannot capture the complex, non-parametric morphologies seen in high-resolution observations, limiting their ability to control shear systematics at the precision required for Roman weak lensing analyses.
AI.method: JWST/NIRCam multi-band observations from GOODS-S and GOODS-N fields are transformed to Roman observing conditions via PSF matching, pixel-scale conversion, and interloper masking preserving correlated noise. A denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) is trained on these data to generate multi-band galaxy postage stamps in Roman Y, J, and H filters. Validation uses an independent dataset with a consistent photometric pipeline comparing magnitude, size, ellipticity, peak surface brightness, and three-band colors.
AI.result: The diffusion model reproduces both marginal distributions and covariance structure of galaxy properties. Only modest deviations occur in low-occupancy regions of parameter space.
AI.conclusion: Diffusion models provide a scalable, physically motivated alternative to analytic simulations for generating high-fidelity galaxy populations, enabling Roman weak lensing calibration and survey preparation for upcoming cosmological experiments.

title: Analysis of a Septuple Open Cluster System and Its Extended Family in Gaia DR3
summary: A rare multiple open cluster system has been analyzed using Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry data. Using Agglomerative Hierarchical clustering and Bayesian-HDBSCAN, we identify a compact core consisting of seven known open clusters and two additional components, including a new candidate, forming a nine-member association. Membership probabilities are refined through statistical modeling, combining GUMM, Bayesian-KDE, and Bayesian-XDGMM for tidal tails identification. Backward orbital integrations confirm coherent motions over 20-30 million years, suggesting a common origin from the same massive molecular cloud. This system offers a unique laboratory for investigating cluster multiplicity, dynamical evolution, and Galactic structure.

AI.tldr: Using Gaia DR3 data and clustering algorithms (HDBSCAN, GUMM, Bayesian-KDE, XDGMM), a rare multiple open cluster system is identified with nine members (including a new candidate). Backward orbital integrations confirm common origin over 20-30 Myr, providing insights into cluster multiplicity and Galactic dynamics.
AI.motivation: To analyze a rare multiple open cluster system using Gaia DR3 data to uncover its structure, membership, and dynamical origin.
AI.method: Combined Agglomerative Hierarchical clustering, Bayesian-HDBSCAN, GUMM, Bayesian-KDE, and Bayesian-XDGMM for membership refinement and tidal tail identification; backward orbital integrations for dynamical coherence analysis.
AI.result: Identified a nine-member association (seven known open clusters plus two additional components, one new candidate) with coherent motions over 20-30 Myr.
AI.conclusion: The system likely originated from the same massive molecular cloud, offering a unique laboratory for studying cluster multiplicity and dynamical evolution.

title: The Oort Cloud as a Gravitational Detector for Primordial Black Holes
summary: Planetary systems can act as sensitive gravitational detectors for dark matter. We investigate the gravitational scattering of Oort cloud objects by primordial black holes (PBHs) as a potential component of the Galactic dark matter halo. Calculating the rates at which PBH encounters eject objects from the Oort cloud or inject them into Earth crossing orbits, we find a linear scaling $Γ\propto m_{\mathrm{PBH}}$ for $m_{\mathrm{PBH}} \gtrsim 10^{-10} M_\odot$. For $m_{\mathrm{PBH}} \sim 10^3 M_\odot$, PBHs constituting all local dark matter would eject $\sim1.3\times10^{12}$ objects over the Solar System's lifetime, comparable to the total Oort cloud population and inject $\sim2.6\times10^{10}$ objects into Earth-crossing orbits. Comparing these rates with observational constraints from long period comet fluxes and terrestrial impact records, we derive upper limits on the PBH dark matter fraction $f_{\mathrm{PBH}}$. Our most stringent constraints exclude $f_{\mathrm{PBH}}=1$ for $10^2 M_\odot \lesssim m_{\mathrm{PBH}} \lesssim 10^5 M_\odot$, with $f_{\mathrm{PBH}} \lesssim 0.002$ at $m_{\mathrm{PBH}} = 10^3 M_\odot$. For the asteroid mass window ($10^{17}$-$10^{23}$ g), scattering rates are far too low to produce observable effects. These Solar System-based constraints complement existing astrophysical probes and demonstrate that planetary systems can serve as sensitive gravitational detectors for compact dark matter.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates how gravitational scattering of Oort cloud objects by primordial black holes (PBHs) can constrain PBHs as dark matter. PBHs eject or inject Oort cloud objects, with rates scaling linearly with PBH mass. For PBHs constituting all local dark matter, ~10^12 Oort cloud objects would be ejected and ~10^10 injected into Earth-crossing orbits. Comparing with comet and impact records yields upper limits: f_PBH=1 excluded for 10^2-10^5 solar masses, f_PBH≲0.002 at peak sensitivity. Asteroid-mass PBHs produce negligible effects.
AI.motivation: To use planetary systems, specifically the Oort cloud, as sensitive gravitational detectors for primordial black hole dark matter, complementing existing astrophysical probes.
AI.method: Calculate scattering rates of Oort cloud objects by PBH encounters, deriving ejection and injection rates as functions of PBH mass. Compare with observational constraints from long-period comet fluxes and terrestrial impact records to set upper limits on the PBH dark matter fraction.
AI.result: Ejection/injection rates scale linearly with PBH mass for m_PBH≳10^-10 M⊙. For m_PBH~10^3 M⊙, PBHs at f_PBH=1 would eject ~1.3×10^12 Oort objects and inject ~2.6×10^10 into Earth-crossing orbits. Most stringent constraints exclude f_PBH=1 for 10^2-10^5 M⊙, with f_PBH≲0.002 at m_PBH=10^3 M⊙. Asteroid-mass PBHs (10^17-10^23 g) yield negligible scattering rates.
AI.conclusion: Solar System-based constraints from Oort cloud scattering provide a powerful complementary probe of PBH dark matter, particularly in the mass range 10^2-10^5 solar masses, demonstrating that planetary systems can serve as sensitive gravitational detectors for compact dark matter.

title: Hessian-based photometric substructure as an evolutionary tracer of OB cluster candidates in M31
summary: Using \textit{Hubble Space Telescope} images from the PHAT and PHAST surveys, we construct an updated catalogue of 747 OB cluster (OBC) candidates. We introduce a dimensionless structural metric, the trace coefficient of variation ($CV_{\rm tr}$), derived from the Hessian matrix in four \textit{HST} bands, to quantify the internal photometric substructure of partially resolved OBC candidates. Cross-matching with the subset of M31 clusters that have independent colour--magnitude diagram (CMD) age estimates yields 247 objects in common. We find statistically significant anti-correlations between $CV_{\rm tr}$ and age in the UV and blue bands, suggesting a progressive smoothing of the light distribution as clusters evolve. Bootstrap resampling confirms the robustness of these trends. Forward modelling of synthetic clusters analysed with the same pipeline recovers a monotonic $CV_{\rm tr}$--age relation under simplified but physically motivated assumptions. These results show that second-order photometric structure contains measurable evolutionary information within the CMD-calibrated regime ($\sim10$--300~Myr).

AI.tldr: Using HST images from PHAT and PHAST surveys, we construct a catalogue of 747 OB cluster candidates in M31, introduce a structural metric (CV_tr) from Hessian matrix analysis, and find anti-correlations between CV_tr and age (10–300 Myr), showing that second-order photometric structure encodes evolutionary information.
AI.motivation: To develop a quantitative metric for internal photometric substructure of partially resolved OB clusters and test whether this substructure correlates with cluster age, enabling evolutionary inferences from imaging data alone without full CMD analysis.
AI.method: Constructed OB cluster catalogue from HST/PHAT+PHAST images; defined CV_tr from Hessian matrix eigenvalues across four HST bands; cross-matched with CMD-dated M31 clusters (N=247); used bootstrap resampling and forward modelling of synthetic clusters to validate trends.
AI.result: Significant anti-correlations between CV_tr and age found in UV/blue bands, robust to bootstrap resampling; forward modelling recovers a monotonic CV_tr–age relation under simplified assumptions.
AI.conclusion: Second-order photometric structure contains measurable evolutionary information in the CMD-calibrated regime (~10–300 Myr), offering a new way to infer cluster ages from structural metrics alone.

title: Cosmological evolution of interacting dark energy with a CPL equation of state
summary: This paper examines interacting dark energy models within the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) parametrization, emphasizing both theoretical structure and observational viability. Two commonly adopted interaction terms are considered: $Q = βH ρ_{de}$ and $Q = βH ρ_c$. We derive exact analytic solutions that describe how the dark sector evolves. These solutions involve incomplete gamma functions and reveal a non-trivial mathematical structure that is often missed in numerical analyses. We perform a Bayesian analysis using current cosmological observations, including the Hubble parameter (OHD), Type Ia supernovae (SNIa), baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), and cosmic microwave background (CMB) data. Relative to the non-interacting CPL scenario, the interacting model with $Q = βH ρ_{de}$ yields a modestly improved fit, as indicated by the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC). However, the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) penalizes increased model complexity, leading to a continued preference for $Λ$CDM. In contrast, the interaction model that depends on dark matter density does not provide observational support. The preferred interacting scenario indicates that the dark energy equation of state evolves dynamically, transitioning from an effective phantom regime at high redshift to quintessence-like behavior at late times. Further analysis indicates the potential for a transient phase of cosmic acceleration in the future. These findings suggest that interacting dark energy models within the CPL framework enrich the standard cosmological model by introducing more diverse phenomenology while maintaining consistency with current observations.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes interacting dark energy models using the CPL parametrization, deriving exact analytic solutions with incomplete gamma functions and performing Bayesian analysis with observational data (OHD, SNIa, BAO, CMB). The Q=βHρ_de model offers modestly improved fit over non-interacting CPL (supported by AIC but penalized by BIC), while the dark matter-dependent interaction lacks observational support. The preferred model shows dynamic dark energy evolving from phantom to quintessence-like behavior with potential transient future acceleration.
AI.motivation: To explore interacting dark energy models within the CPL parametrization framework, deriving exact analytic solutions beyond numerical approximations, and assessing their observational viability against current cosmological data.
AI.method: Exact analytic solutions involving incomplete gamma functions; Bayesian parameter estimation using OHD, SNIa, BAO, and CMB data; model comparison via AIC and BIC.
AI.result: The Q=βHρ_de model yields a modestly improved fit over non-interacting CPL per AIC, but BIC penalizes complexity, favoring ΛCDM. The Q=βHρ_c model lacks observational support. The preferred model indicates dynamical dark energy transitioning from phantom to quintessence-like behavior with potential transient future acceleration.
AI.conclusion: Interacting dark energy models within CPL enrich standard cosmology with diverse phenomenology (phantom-to-quintessence transition, transient acceleration) while remaining consistent with current observations, though Bayesian criteria still favor simpler ΛCDM.

title: The Dependence of the Mean Spectral Energy Distributions on the Accretion Rate for Quasars with $z < 0.75$ from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey
comment: 24 pages, 8 figures, Accepted for publication in ApJS
summary: We construct mean spectral energy distributions (SEDs) for a substantial sample of 56,969 Sloan Digital Sky Survey DR16 quasars with $z < 0.75$, utilizing multiwavelength data from the mid-infrared (MIR) to ultraviolet (UV). These SEDs are built on eigenvector 1 parameters -- the relative optical $\rm Fe~ II$ strength ($R_{\rm Fe~II}$) and the H$β$ line width ($\rm Hβ$) -- that capture the principal spectral variance of quasar spectra. From three $R_{\rm Fe~II}$-dependent mean SEDs we find that quasars with a larger $R_{\rm Fe~II}$ exhibit redder UV and optical and redder MIR and near-infrared (NIR) continua, indicating more dust emission. We also split our sample directly into Eddington ratio $L_{\rm Bol} /L_{\rm Edd}$ (or dimensionless accretion rate $\dot{\mathscr{M}}$) bins to construct different mean SEDs and find that the continua become increasingly red with increasing $L_{\rm Bol} /L_{\rm Edd}$ (or $\dot{\mathscr{M}}$) in the MIR, NIR, and UV bands. This demonstrates that the shapes of Type 1 AGN SEDs depend on the accretion rate. However, the optical continuum shows the opposite trend (becoming harder and bluer), indicating the complexity of the optical emission region. From $\rm FWHM_{Hβ}$-dependent mean SEDs we find that quasars with a larger $\rm FWHM_{Hβ}$ show redder optical and NIR continua and bluer UV and MIR continua. The bluer MIR continuum suggests that a larger angle between of the line of sight and the torus plane results in weaker torus emission in the MIR.

AI.tldr: This paper constructs mean SEDs for 56,969 SDSS DR16 quasars (z<0.75) using eigenvector 1 parameters (R_FeII and Hβ line width). Results show that higher R_FeII (stronger Fe II) correlates with redder UV-to-MIR continua; higher Eddington ratio yields redder MIR/NIR/UV but bluer optical continua; broader Hβ correlates with redder optical/NIR but bluer UV/MIR continua, suggesting orientation effects on torus emission.
AI.motivation: To understand how quasar spectral energy distributions depend on key physical parameters such as Fe II strength, accretion rate, and orientation, which are captured by eigenvector 1 parameters.
AI.method: Construct mean SEDs for 56,969 SDSS DR16 quasars (z<0.75) using multiwavelength data from MIR to UV, binned by R_FeII, Eddington ratio (L_Bol/L_Edd or dimensionless accretion rate), and FWHM_Hβ.
AI.result: Higher R_FeII quasars show redder UV-to-MIR continua. Higher accretion rate quasars show redder MIR/NIR/UV but bluer optical continua. Broader Hβ quasars show redder optical/NIR but bluer UV/MIR continua, with bluer MIR suggesting larger viewing angle relative to torus plane.
AI.conclusion: Type 1 AGN SED shapes depend on accretion rate and orientation, with complex behavior in the optical emission region and torus emission influenced by viewing angle.

title: Parametric Resonance in $φ^4$ Preheating: An Exact Numerical Study
summary: Preheating after inflation proceeds through parametric resonance, leading to efficient particle production in scalar field models. In this work, we investigate the structure of parametric resonance in the $φ^4$ chaotic inflationary model during the preheating phase by performing a fully numerical analysis of the coupled dynamical equations governing the inflaton field and the mode function of the produced particles, thereby avoiding the approximations commonly employed in earlier studies. Our results reveal resonance patterns that differ significantly from those obtained with approximate analytical treatments. In the weak coupling regime, short-wavelength modes rapidly settle into oscillations with nearly constant amplitude, while the corresponding occupation numbers approach saturation. However, the long-wavelength modes exhibit gradual amplitude growth, with occupation numbers transitioning into a non-linear oscillatory regime. As the coupling strength increases, the dynamics becomes increasingly nonlinear, leading to the emergence of stochastic behavior. In the strong coupling regime, short-wavelength modes display a step-like (staircase) evolution in the occupation number, indicative of intermittent bursts of particle production. However, the long-wavelength modes exhibit a more gradual, monotonic growth with small superimposed fluctuations. These findings highlight the rich, coupling-dependent, structure of parametric resonance in the quartic inflationary model and underscore the importance of exact numerical treatment in accurately capturing preheating dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper numerically analyzes parametric resonance during preheating in the φ⁴ chaotic inflationary model, revealing coupling-dependent resonance patterns that differ from approximate analytical treatments, including amplitude saturation for short-wavelength modes and staircase-like occupation number evolution in strong coupling.
AI.motivation: To accurately capture the structure of parametric resonance in the φ⁴ inflationary model during preheating, avoiding approximations used in earlier studies that may miss important nonlinear dynamics.
AI.method: Fully numerical analysis of the coupled dynamical equations governing the inflaton field and the mode function of produced particles, without relying on common approximations.
AI.result: Short-wavelength modes settle into nearly constant amplitude oscillations with saturated occupation numbers in weak coupling, while long-wavelength modes show gradual growth with nonlinear oscillations. Strong coupling induces stochastic behavior and step-like (staircase) evolution in short-wavelength occupation numbers, with monotonic growth for long-wavelength modes.
AI.conclusion: Parametric resonance in the quartic inflationary model exhibits rich, coupling-dependent structure, and exact numerical treatment is essential for accurately capturing preheating dynamics.

title: A graph-based Neural Network surrogate model for accelerating semi-analytical model of galaxy formation and evolution
summary: Understanding how galaxy populations emerge and evolve from the growth of dark matter structure is a central challenge in galaxy formation theory. Semi-analytic models (SAMs) provide an efficient framework to address this problem, but exploring large ensembles of merger trees across broad parameter spaces remains computationally demanding. We develop a conditional graph neural network surrogate model that combines merger tree information with SAM parameters to predict galaxy properties across cosmic time. Using merger trees of dark matter halos from the Uchuu simulation and the Galacticus SAM, the model predicts stellar mass, luminosity, angular momentum, gas metal mass, and specific star formation rate across the wide redshift range of 0 <= z <= 5. For instance, the model can predict stellar mass at 0 <= z <= 3 with a scatter of 0.19-0.28 dex and coefficient of determination R^2 of 0.946-0.973 (R^2 close to 1 indicates prediction closely matching the truth). The results show that a single graph based model can reproduce these galaxy properties with good accuracy over multiple SAM realizations, merger trees and redshifts. This catalog-level model provides a practical route for accelerating SAM based studies of galaxy formation to enable a more detailed investigation of the model parameter space. The inference code, trained models, and example data products are publicly available at https://github.com/MutongCat/sam2galaxy-gnn.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a conditional graph neural network surrogate model that combines dark matter merger tree information with semi-analytic model (SAM) parameters to predict galaxy properties (stellar mass, luminosity, angular momentum, gas metal mass, specific star formation rate) across redshift 0 ≤ z ≤ 5, achieving high accuracy (e.g., stellar mass R² of 0.946-0.973 at z≤3) while significantly accelerating SAM-based galaxy formation studies.
AI.motivation: Understanding how galaxy populations emerge from dark matter structure growth is a central challenge in galaxy formation theory. SAMs provide an efficient framework but exploring large ensembles of merger trees across broad parameter spaces remains computationally demanding, motivating the need for a faster surrogate model.
AI.method: A conditional graph neural network surrogate model is developed that combines merger tree information from dark matter halos (Uchuu simulation) with SAM parameters (Galacticus SAM) to predict galaxy properties. The model operates as a catalog-level graph-based approach across multiple SAM realizations and redshifts.
AI.result: The model predicts stellar mass, luminosity, angular momentum, gas metal mass, and specific star formation rate across 0 ≤ z ≤ 5. For stellar mass at 0 ≤ z ≤ 3, it achieves scatter of 0.19-0.28 dex and R² of 0.946-0.973, demonstrating good accuracy over multiple SAM realizations, merger trees, and redshifts.
AI.conclusion: A single graph-based model can reproduce galaxy properties with good accuracy, providing a practical route for accelerating SAM-based studies of galaxy formation and enabling more detailed investigation of the model parameter space. Code, trained models, and example data are publicly released.

title: Testing Scalar Field Dark Matter models in M31 galaxy through the Rotation Curve analysis
summary: We explore the viability of scalar field dark matter halo models through the rotation curve analysis of the Andromeda galaxy (M31), taking into account a realistic description of its baryonic structure. The mass model includes a stellar disk described by the Freeman profile and two alternative bulge configurations: a classical single de Vaucouleurs bulge and a two-component structure consisting of inner and main bulges modeled by exponential sphere profiles. The dark matter halo is modeled using three scalar field motivated models: fuzzy dark matter (FDM), Bose-Einstein condensate and multistate scalar-field dark matter. The model parameters are determined through the Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares fitting, and the relative performance of the models is evaluated using the Bayesian Information Criterion which allows a direct comparison with previous phenomenological halo studies performed for the same galaxy. We find that the two-bulge baryonic configuration ensures a better statistical description of the M31 rotation curve, independently of the adopted halo model. The results also suggest that, within scalar field dark matter scenarios, smooth cored halos, such as FDM, provide the most consistent description of the M31 kinematics.

AI.tldr: This paper tests scalar field dark matter halo models (FDM, Bose-Einstein condensate, multistate) against the M31 rotation curve, finding that a two-bulge baryonic configuration and smooth cored halos (especially FDM) best describe the kinematics.
AI.motivation: To explore the viability of scalar field dark matter halo models for M31 using realistic baryonic structures, enabling direct comparison with previous phenomenological halo studies.
AI.method: Mass models include a Freeman-profile stellar disk and two bulge configurations (classical de Vaucouleurs bulge vs. two-component exponential sphere bulges). Dark matter halo is modeled with fuzzy dark matter (FDM), Bose-Einstein condensate, and multistate scalar-field dark matter. Parameters are fitted via Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear least-squares; model comparison uses the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC).
AI.result: The two-bulge baryonic configuration outperforms the single bulge across all halo models. Among scalar field models, smooth cored halos (particularly FDM) provide the most consistent description of M31's rotation curve.
AI.conclusion: Scalar field dark matter models are viable for M31; FDM with a two-bulge baryonic model yields the best statistical fit to the observed kinematics.

title: STVG-MOG Cluster Dynamics and the Cosmological $1/r^2$ Force Law from Pairwise kSZ Data
summary: We investigate whether Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity in its weak-field modified gravity form can account for the cluster-scale inverse-square force law inferred from recent kinematic Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements of cluster pairwise motions. The starting point is the X-COP cluster fit of STVG-MOG, for which a representative baryonic cluster mass $M\sim 10^{15}M_\odot$ together with parameters $α\sim 9.11$ and $μ\sim 0.196~{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ provides a successful description of cluster dynamics without particle dark matter. We extrapolate this fit to the separation range $30$ to $230~{\rm Mpc}$, relevant for the pairwise kSZ analysis. Since the Yukawa transition length $μ^{-1}\simeq 5.1~{\rm Mpc}$ is much smaller than these separations, the STVG-MOG acceleration law reduces to an effective inverse-square form. This explains why the theory can satisfy the observed Newtonian behavior while remaining distinct from MOND-like long-distance modifications. We derive the corresponding pairwise velocity curve and show that, after fitting a single overall kSZ amplitude, the extrapolated STVG-MOG prediction reproduces the measured trend of the pairwise kSZ data. The analysis shows that the X-COP cluster fit and the cosmological-scale kSZ force-law result are mutually consistent within STVG-MOG.

AI.tldr: The paper shows that STVG-MOG (Scalar-Tensor-Vector Gravity) can simultaneously explain cluster-scale dynamics (X-COP fit) and cosmological-scale pairwise motions (kSZ measurements) without dark matter, because at large separations (30–230 Mpc) the Yukawa correction decays into an effective inverse-square law, making it consistent with Newtonian behavior.
AI.motivation: To test whether STVG-MOG, a modified gravity theory that successfully fits cluster-scale dynamics without dark matter, remains consistent with the inverse-square force law observed at larger cosmological scales via pairwise kSZ cluster motions.
AI.method: Take the X-COP cluster fit parameters (M ~ 10¹⁵ M⊙, α ≈ 9.11, μ ≈ 0.196 Mpc⁻¹) and extrapolate to separations 30–230 Mpc. Because the Yukawa scale μ⁻¹ ≈ 5.1 Mpc is much smaller than these separations, the acceleration reduces to an effective Newtonian inverse-square form. The pairwise velocity curve is then computed and compared to kSZ data after fitting a single amplitude parameter.
AI.result: The extrapolated STVG-MOG prediction reproduces the measured trend of pairwise kSZ data after fitting a single overall amplitude. The X-COP cluster-scale fit and the cosmological-scale kSZ force-law result are mutually consistent within this theory.
AI.conclusion: STVG-MOG can simultaneously describe cluster dynamics without dark matter and comply with the observed Newtonian inverse-square law at large separations, distinguishing itself from MOND-like long-distance modifications.

title: Two Exciting High-redshift Galaxy Candidates Turn Out to Be Two Exciting Ultra-cool Brown Dwarfs
summary: From the onset of observations of JWST we have discovered unexpectedly luminous galaxies at redshifts $z>10$ and as high as $z=14$. With their discovery, the question immediately followed as to where their progenitors are, since such progenitors should be within reach of existing surveys. However, the discovery of several bright candidates at $z>15$ may indicate further discrepancies between pre-JWST model predictions and current observations. Progenitors of the bright $z\sim 14$ galaxies should be visible at redshifts as high as $z\sim 20$--$30$, showing in the data as F356W and F277W dropouts. We identify two such candidates in the Bullet Cluster JWST data; however, subsequent NIRSpec follow-up data show spectra that can be well fit with ultra-cool Y dwarf templates with temperatures $T_{\rm eff} = 350^{+110}_{-80}\,\mbox{K}$ and $T_{\rm eff} = 410^{+110}_{-50}\,\mbox{K}$ and distances of $\sim 500\,\mbox{pc}$. The first is one of the lowest temperature brown dwarfs known spectroscopically. With additional NIRCam imaging taken $\sim 1$ year later, we also detect their proper motions of $(49 \pm 8)\,\mbox{mas/yr}$ and $(24 \pm 3)\,\mbox{mas/yr}$, further indicating that at least some F277W and F356W dropouts are sub-stellar cold Milky Way objects such as brown dwarfs. We find a sky density of 0.14 Y dwarfs per arcmin$^2$ and caution that the probability of detecting such objects may increase significantly in surveys at low galactic latitudes.

AI.tldr: JWST observations of high-redshift galaxy candidates (z~14) initially suggested progenitors at z~20-30, identified as F356W/F277W dropouts in Bullet Cluster data. However, NIRSpec follow-up revealed these are actually ultra-cool Y dwarfs (T_eff ~350-410 K) at ~500 pc distance, with proper motions confirming their substellar nature. This highlights contamination of high-z galaxy searches by cold Milky Way brown dwarfs.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether F356W/F277W dropouts, initially interpreted as progenitors of bright z~14 galaxies, are truly high-redshift objects, and to understand discrepancies between pre-JWST model predictions and observations of luminous galaxies at z>10.
AI.method: Identification of F356W/F277W dropout candidates in Bullet Cluster JWST data, followed by NIRSpec spectroscopic follow-up and comparison with Y dwarf atmospheric models. Proper motion analysis using multi-epoch NIRCam imaging separated by ~1 year.
AI.result: Spectra of the two candidates are well-fit by ultra-cool Y dwarf templates (T_eff = 350^+110_-80 K and 410^+110_-50 K) at ~500 pc. Proper motions of 49±8 mas/yr and 24±3 mas/yr confirm they are substellar Milky Way objects, not high-z galaxies. Sky density of Y dwarfs is ~0.14 per arcmin².
AI.conclusion: At least some F277W/F356W dropouts are cold brown dwarfs, not high-redshift galaxy progenitors. Surveys at low galactic latitudes have increased probability of such contamination, requiring spectroscopic follow-up or proper motion analysis to distinguish substellar objects from true high-z candidates.

title: The open-Universe signal: A model artifact rather than genuine curvature
summary: Recent late-Universe observations suggest an open Universe. If confirmed, such a departure from spatial flatness would carry profound implications for our understanding of cosmic inflation and the ultimate fate of the Universe. Motivated by this intriguing result and the release of new data, we revisit the question using baryon acoustic oscillation measurements from DESI DR2, multiple Type Ia supernova samples, refined strong gravitational lensing time-delay analyses, and the most up-to-date cosmic chronometer data. We find that within the $Λ$ cold dark matter ($Λ$CDM) paradigm, the combined data still prefer an open Universe with $Ω_K=0.049\pm0.037$. However, this preference vanishes in extensions to $Λ$CDM, where the data instead favor a flat Universe. The model comparison shows that for $Λ$CDM, introducing new physics is preferred over merely allowing spatial curvature, and flat $Λ$CDM extensions perform better than their curved counterparts. We therefore argue that the mild open-Universe signal is an artifact of limited model flexibility, rather than a genuine feature of late-Universe observations.

AI.tldr: The paper investigates the recent observational hint of an open (negatively curved) Universe. Using DESI DR2 BAO, supernovae, strong lensing time delays, and cosmic chronometer data, the authors find a mild preference for an open Universe within ΛCDM (Ω_K=0.049±0.037), but this preference disappears in extended models, where flat Universe is favored. Model comparison indicates that the open-Universe signal is an artifact of limited model flexibility, not a genuine feature.
AI.motivation: Recent late-Universe observations suggest an open Universe, which—if real—would challenge cosmic inflation and alter predictions for the Universe's ultimate fate. The authors are motivated to re-examine this question using the latest data (DESI DR2, new SNe, lensing, cosmic chronometers).
AI.method: The authors combine baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) measurements from DESI DR2, multiple Type Ia supernova samples, refined strong gravitational lensing time-delay analyses, and up-to-date cosmic chronometer data. They test both ΛCDM and extended models (beyond ΛCDM) to assess the robustness of the open-Universe signal.
AI.result: Within ΛCDM, the combined data prefer an open Universe with Ω_K=0.049±0.037 (mild preference). However, in extensions to ΛCDM, the data favor flat Universe. Model comparison shows that introducing new physics (beyond ΛCDM) is preferred over adding spatial curvature, and flat ΛCDM extensions perform better than curved ones.
AI.conclusion: The mild open-Universe signal is an artifact of limited model flexibility rather than a genuine feature of late-Universe observations. The preference for an open Universe disappears when extended models are considered.

title: The Vertical Structure and Asymmetry of Mg ii-enriched Gas in the Milky Way Disk
comment: 18 pages, 11 figures and 3 tables, Accepted by SCPMA
summary: The physical properties of Milky Way Mgii-bearing gas remain poorly constrained due to the saturation of the near-UV doublet. We utilize the weaker Mgii $λλ$1239, 1240 doublet from 482 archival HST/COS extragalactic sightlines to probe this cool gas phase. We identify 43 low-velocity absorbers ($|v_{\rm LSR}|<40\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$), yielding a covering fraction ($C_f$) of $32\pm5\%$ for $\log N_{\rm MgII} > 15$. We find that $C_f$ follows an exponential decay relative to equivalent width thresholds, marking a transition from a diffuse medium to localized, dense structures (e.g., cold neutral medium cores). The steep decline of the distribution at high column densities likely reflects the saturation of the turbulent log-normal spectrum and dust depletion. By integrating stellar data, we derive a Mgii scale height $h_{\rm MgII} = 0.12\pm0.02\ \rm\ kpc$ and mid-plane density $n_{0,\rm MgII} = (3.9\pm0.4)\times 10^{-6}\ \rm cm^{-3}$. A pronounced north-south asymmetry exists, with the northern hemisphere displaying a significantly higher mid-plane density ($n_{0,n} \approx 4.7 \times 10^{-6}\ \rm cm^{-3}$) than the south ($3.2 \times 10^{-6}\ \rm cm^{-3}$). This discrepancy suggests that the northern interstellar medium is more spatially concentrated and clumpy, whereas the southern gas is more ubiquitously distributed with a lower average density. These results indicate that Mgii is tightly confined to the disk, governed by a unified depletion law and restricted vertical extent.

AI.tldr: Using 482 HST/COS sightlines, this study identifies 43 low-velocity MgII absorbers via the weaker λλ1239,1240 doublet, finding a covering fraction of 32±5% for log N_MgII > 15, a scale height of 0.12±0.02 kpc, and a north-south asymmetry in mid-plane density.
AI.motivation: The physical properties of Milky Way MgII-bearing gas remain poorly constrained due to saturation of the near-UV doublet, motivating the use of the weaker MgII λλ1239,1240 doublet to probe this cool gas phase.
AI.method: Utilized the weaker MgII λλ1239,1240 doublet from 482 archival HST/COS extragalactic sightlines to identify low-velocity absorbers, measured covering fractions as a function of equivalent width thresholds, and integrated stellar data to derive scale height and mid-plane density.
AI.result: Identified 43 low-velocity absorbers with Cf=32±5% for log N_MgII > 15; derived h_MgII = 0.12±0.02 kpc and n0,MgII = (3.9±0.4)×10⁻⁶ cm⁻³; found pronounced north-south asymmetry with northern mid-plane density (4.7×10⁻⁶ cm⁻³) higher than southern (3.2×10⁻⁶ cm⁻³).
AI.conclusion: MgII is tightly confined to the disk, governed by a unified depletion law and restricted vertical extent; the covering fraction's exponential decay marks a transition from diffuse medium to localized dense structures, with the steep decline at high column densities reflecting turbulent log-normal spectrum saturation and dust depletion.

title: CLASH-VLT: The Fifth Force in Chameleon Gravity from Joint Lensing and Kinematics Cluster Mass Profiles
comment: 24 pages, 9 figures. Published in Universe for the Special Issue Celebrating the 110th Anniversary of General Relativity: Advances, Challenges and Perspectives
summary: We present a high-precision joint gravitational-lensing and kinematic analysis of nine massive galaxy clusters from the CLASH and CLASH-VLT surveys to test chameleon screening gravity and its $f(R)$ sub-class at Mpc scales. We investigate the dependence on the assumed parametrization of the total cluster mass profile by adopting three models, namely Navarro--Frenk--White (NFW), Burkert, and Hernquist. When cuspy models (NFW or Hernquist) are assumed in the general chameleon framework, the combined constraints from the nine clusters are fully consistent with General Relativity (GR), excluding large regions of the modified-gravity parameter space (the coupling constant $\mathcal{Q}$ and the background chameleon field $ φ_\infty$), providing one of the tightest bounds on general chameleon models with clusters to date. In contrast, adopting a Burkert profile -- disfavored by lensing data -- leads to a mild ($\sim 2σ$) departure from the GR expectation in joint analysis. When considering the $f(R)$ sub-case, we obtain a bound on the background scalaron field of $|f_R| \lesssim \mathrm{2-5}\times 10^{-5}$ (95\% C.L.) for NFW and Hernquist models, in agreement with current constraints at cosmological scales, and an apparent deviation from standard gravity of $\log_{10}|f_R| = -4.7 \pm 1.2$ for the Burkert case. We investigate the impact of systematics in the kinematical analysis, showing that the tension is mitigated when clusters exhibiting clear dynamical disturbance are excluded from the sample. [...[ The upcoming generation of wide-field lensing surveys and spectroscopic follow-up programs will enable similar analyses on substantially larger samples, offering the prospect of tightening cluster-based constraints on gravity and the dark sector.

AI.tldr: This paper tests chameleon screening gravity and f(R) gravity using gravitational-lensing and kinematic data from nine massive galaxy clusters in the CLASH and CLASH-VLT surveys. Using NFW, Burkert, and Hernquist mass profiles, the authors find that cuspy models (NFW, Hernquist) are consistent with General Relativity and yield tight constraints on modified gravity parameters, while the Burkert profile (disfavored by lensing) shows a mild ~2σ deviation. For f(R) gravity, bounds on |f_R| are ~2-5×10^{-5} (95% C.L.) for NFW/Hernquist, consistent with cosmological constraints. Systematics from dynamically disturbed clusters can mitigate apparent tensions.
AI.motivation: To test chameleon screening gravity and its f(R) subclass at Mpc scales using massive galaxy clusters, providing constraints on modified gravity parameter space and testing consistency with General Relativity.
AI.method: Joint gravitational-lensing and kinematic analysis of nine massive galaxy clusters from CLASH and CLASH-VLT surveys, using three mass profile parametrizations (NFW, Burkert, Hernquist) within the chameleon framework.
AI.result: NFW and Hernquist profiles are fully consistent with GR, yielding tight bounds on chameleon parameters and f(R) scalaron field |f_R| ≲ 2-5×10^{-5} (95% C.L.). Burkert profile shows a mild (~2σ) deviation from GR, but tension is mitigated when dynamically disturbed clusters are excluded.
AI.conclusion: The study provides some of the tightest cluster-based bounds on chameleon models to date. Results highlight the importance of mass profile assumptions and systematics in testing modified gravity. Future wide-field surveys will enable stronger constraints.

title: A GLIMPSE of the 99%: a census of the faintest galaxies during the epoch reionization and its implications for galaxy formation models
summary: We present a comprehensive study of the galaxy UV luminosity function (UVLF) at $z=6-9$ leveraging deep JWST observations from the GLIMPSE survey. Thanks to gravitational lensing, we probe the UVLF to an unprecedented depth of $M_{\text{UV}} = -12$ mag, approximately three magnitudes deeper than previous robust constraints. Our UVLF determination incorporates a rigorous end-to-end uncertainty framework, including statistical and systematic lensing uncertainties. We find that the $z \sim 7$ UVLF continues to rise steeply with a faint-end slope of $α= -1.98_{-0.05}^{+0.06}$. Crucially, our data show no clear evidence of a turnover down to \muv $= -12.3$. The persistence of this faint population provides stringent constraints on galaxy formation models and cosmological simulations that predict an early flattening of the luminosity function due to radiative feedback or star-formation thresholds. Furthermore, post-JWST models specifically calibrated to match the UV-bright excess at $z > 10$ generally fail to reproduce the observed evolution toward lower redshifts and fainter magnitudes, highlighting a significant tension in our current understanding of early galaxy assembly. We derive a comoving ionizing emissivity at $z=7$ of log($n_{\mathrm ion}$ / s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-3}$) $\approx 50.85$, which suggests that faint galaxies dominate the ionizing budget, providing enough photons to maintain reionization even in a highly clumped IGM ($C_{\text{HII}} = 5$). As our detection of faint galaxies effectively rules out a luminosity function truncation at $M_{\text{UV}} \geq -15$, these results emphasize the need to either accurately characterize the ionizing properties of the global, low-mass galaxy population at $z > 6$, or to refine physical models of intergalactic medium clumping and its redshift evolution to maintain consistency with the observed reionization timeline.

AI.tldr: This paper presents JWST GLIMPSE survey measurements of the galaxy UV luminosity function at z=6–9 down to M_UV = −12 mag via gravitational lensing. The faint-end slope at z~7 is α = −1.98, with no turnover observed. The results challenge current galaxy formation models and imply faint galaxies dominate the ionizing budget, maintaining reionization.
AI.motivation: To extend the UV luminosity function to unprecedented faint magnitudes (M_UV = −12) at z=6–9 using JWST, and test whether the UVLF exhibits a turnover at faint luminosities, which would constrain galaxy formation physics and the ionizing contribution of low-mass galaxies to cosmic reionization.
AI.method: Deep JWST observations from the GLIMPSE survey combined with gravitational lensing to probe down to M_UV = −12 mag. A rigorous end-to-end uncertainty framework incorporating both statistical and systematic lensing uncertainties was used to determine the UVLF.
AI.result: The faint-end slope at z~7 is α = −1.98^{+0.06}_{−0.05}, with no evidence of a turnover down to M_UV = −12.3. Post-JWST models calibrated to match UV-bright excess at z>10 fail to reproduce the observed evolution toward lower redshifts and fainter magnitudes. Comoving ionizing emissivity at z=7 is log(n_ion / s^{−1} Mpc^{−3}) ≈ 50.85.
AI.conclusion: Faint galaxies dominate the ionizing photon budget and can sustain reionization even in a highly clumped IGM (C_HII = 5). The absence of a UVLF truncation down to M_UV ≥ −15 rules out luminosity function turnover models, requiring either better characterization of low-mass galaxy ionizing properties or revised IGM clumping models to reconcile with the observed reionization timeline.

title: Reconstructing the cosmic expansion with a generalized q(z) parameterization: A decelerating Universe from late-time constraints
comment: Accepted for publication in The European Physical Journal C
summary: We present a generalized phenomenological parameterization of the deceleration parameter $q(z)$ that incorporates an effective radiative component (ERC) in addition to a localized late-time contribution. The proposed framework extends previous two-parameter $q(z)$ reconstructions by explicitly regulating the high-redshift behavior while preserving the late-time transition dynamics. We constrain the free parameters $(h, q_0, z_c, z_e)$ using late-time observational data from cosmic chronometers (CC), Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae (SNIa), H\,\textsc{ii} galaxies (HIIG), and intermediate-luminosity quasars (QSO). For the full data combination (CC+SNIa+HIIG+QSO), we obtain $q_0 = -0.25^{+0.04}_{-0.04}$ and a transition redshift $z_T \simeq 0.80$, indicating a currently accelerating Universe with a transition occurring earlier than in the $Λ$CDM model. Within the redshift range probed by the data, the reconstructed $q(z)$ deviates from the $Λ$CDM trend, suggesting a possible reduction of the late-time acceleration. Furthermore, the reconstruction favors a relatively high value of the Hubble parameter, $h = 0.729 \pm 0.006$. The ERC remains weakly constrained by late-time data but ensures a smooth and monotonic evolution of $q(z)$, $j(z)$, and $w_{\rm eff}(z)$ across a wide redshift range. Within the observed interval, the model effectively reproduces the late-time behavior of the previous parametrization, while providing a controlled extension toward early epochs. Our results show that current low- and intermediate-redshift data are compatible with a reduced late-time acceleration.

AI.tldr: The authors propose a generalized four-parameter phenomenological model of the deceleration parameter $q(z)$ that includes an effective radiative component to regulate high-redshift behavior. Using CC, Pantheon+ SNIa, HIIG, and QSO data, they find $q_0 = -0.25^{+0.04}_{-0.04}$, transition redshift $z_T \simeq 0.80$, and $h = 0.729 \pm 0.006$, suggesting reduced late-time acceleration compared to $\Lambda$CDM.
AI.motivation: To extend existing two-parameter $q(z)$ reconstructions by adding an effective radiative component that explicitly regulates high-redshift behavior while preserving late-time transition dynamics, enabling a more physically consistent parametrization across a wide redshift range.
AI.method: A generalized phenomenological parameterization of $q(z)$ with four free parameters $(h, q_0, z_c, z_e)$, incorporating an effective radiative component (ERC). Constraints are derived using late-time observational data: cosmic chronometers (CC), Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae (SNIa), HII galaxies (HIIG), and intermediate-luminosity quasars (QSO).
AI.result: $q_0 = -0.25^{+0.04}_{-0.04}$, $z_T \simeq 0.80$, $h = 0.729 \pm 0.006$. The reconstructed $q(z)$ deviates from $\Lambda$CDM within the data redshift range, suggesting reduced late-time acceleration. The ERC remains weakly constrained by late-time data but ensures smooth monotonic evolution of $q(z)$, $j(z)$, and $w_{\rm eff}(z)$.
AI.conclusion: Current low- and intermediate-redshift data are compatible with a reduced late-time acceleration compared to $\Lambda$CDM, with an earlier transition redshift. The model provides a controlled extension toward early epochs while reproducing previous parametrization behavior at late times.

title: With arms wide open: a VLT/MUSE view of the mechanisms driving unwinding spiral arms in cluster galaxies
comment: 20 pages, 21 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: The environmental mechanisms driving unwinding spiral arms in cluster galaxies remain debated. While earlier studies attributed it mainly to gravitational interactions, recent works suggest that RPS alone can induce unwinding. We present a VLT/MUSE spatially resolved analysis to investigate the mechanisms responsible for spiral-arm unwinding in two galaxies, UG101 and UG103, drawn from a larger sample. They are selected as tidal and RPS-driven candidates, respectively, based on the proximity of close neighbors. We estimate the galactocentric radius at which tidal forces, from a companion or the cluster potential, become relevant ($R_{\mathrm{tid}}$). We examine gas and stellar kinematics, exploiting their different responses to gravitational and hydrodynamical perturbations. SINOPSIS is used to map stellar populations in age bins and constrain unwinding timescales. For UG101, we find $R_{\mathrm{tid}} \sim 1.5 R_e$, while the unwound features extend beyond this radius. UG101 shows irregular stellar and gas kinematics; its rotation curve indicates similar motions, although the gas is truncated on one side and extended on the other. For UG103, neither the closest companion nor the cluster appear capable of triggering unwinding. UG103 displays regular stellar but disturbed gas kinematics, with truncation on the disk side likely facing the ICM wind and gas extended in the opposite direction. Stellar population maps show the emergence and unwinding of the spiral arms in UG103 on timescales consistent with its cluster infall time ($\sim 1.6$ Gyr). We conclude that unwinding in UG101 and UG103 is primarily driven by tidal interactions and RPS, respectively, although a combined effect cannot be excluded for UG101. Our methodology provides a framework to identify the mechanisms driving unwinding in cluster galaxies from spatially resolved properties.

AI.tldr: This paper uses VLT/MUSE spatially resolved analysis to investigate spiral-arm unwinding in two cluster galaxies (UG101 and UG103), finding that UG101's unwinding is driven by tidal interactions while UG103's is driven by ram pressure stripping, with timescales consistent with cluster infall (~1.6 Gyr).
AI.motivation: The environmental mechanisms driving unwinding spiral arms in cluster galaxies remain debated; earlier studies attributed it to gravitational interactions but recent works suggest ram pressure stripping (RPS) alone can induce unwinding, motivating a need to distinguish between these mechanisms.
AI.method: VLT/MUSE spatially resolved analysis of two galaxies (UG101 and UG103) selected as tidal and RPS-driven candidates respectively; estimation of galactocentric tidal radius (R_tid); examination of gas and stellar kinematics to exploit their different responses to gravitational vs. hydrodynamical perturbations; SINOPSIS stellar population mapping in age bins to constrain unwinding timescales.
AI.result: UG101: R_tid ~ 1.5 R_e with unwound features beyond this radius; irregular stellar and gas kinematics; gas truncated on one side and extended on the other. UG103: neither closest companion nor cluster capable of triggering unwinding; regular stellar but disturbed gas kinematics; gas truncation on the ICM wind-facing side; stellar population maps show unwinding on timescales consistent with cluster infall (~1.6 Gyr).
AI.conclusion: Unwinding in UG101 and UG103 is primarily driven by tidal interactions and RPS respectively, though a combined effect cannot be excluded for UG101. The methodology provides a framework to identify unwinding mechanisms in cluster galaxies from spatially resolved properties.

title: A sound-horizon-free measurement of the Hubble constant from DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations using artificial neural networks
summary: We present a model-independent, sound-horizon-free measurement of the Hubble constant $H_0$ using baryon acoustic oscillation tracers from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Data Release 2. The function reconstructions are performed using the artificial neural network method, which is a completely data-driven approach that avoids the mild $Λ$CDM prior dependence. Our approach is based on the distance duality relation and combines three complementary observational probes, such as Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometer, and DESI DR2 BAO -- without requiring any knowledge of the sound horizon scale $r_d$ or any assumption about the absolute luminosity of SNe Ia. We obtain a joint constraint of $H_0 = 71.5\pm2.2$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$ at 68\% confidence for 1000 bootstrap realisations and 4096 neurons, which is consistent with the TRGB result and the SH0ES measurement within $0.6σ$, consistent with the Planck 2020 result within $2σ$. Our results favor a higher value of $H_0$ compared to the Planck CMB inference, adding independent support for the reality of the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: The paper measures H₀ = 71.5±2.2 km/s/Mpc using DESI DR2 BAO, SNe Ia, and cosmic chronometers via neural network reconstruction, without assuming a sound horizon or ΛCDM prior, supporting the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: To measure H₀ independently of the sound horizon scale and ΛCDM assumptions, addressing model dependence in previous BAO-based H₀ constraints and testing the reality of the Hubble tension.
AI.method: Artificial neural network-based function reconstruction applied to DESI DR2 BAO, Type Ia supernovae, and cosmic chronometer data, leveraging the distance duality relation to avoid sound horizon and absolute luminosity assumptions.
AI.result: H₀ = 71.5±2.2 km/s/Mpc (68% CL) from 1000 bootstrap realizations with 4096 neurons; consistent with TRGB and SH0ES within 0.6σ, and with Planck 2020 within 2σ.
AI.conclusion: The result favors a higher H₀ than Planck CMB inference, providing independent, model-independent evidence supporting the reality of the Hubble tension.

title: East Asian VLBI Network astrometry toward the star-forming region G040.96+02.48 in the Extreme Outer Galaxy
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables, accepted for publication in AJ
summary: Accurate astrometric measurements for star-forming regions located on the far side of the Milky Way remain scarce. In this work, we present the astrometric results for a 22\,GHz water maser associated with star-forming region G040.96+02.48 located on the far side of the Milky Way, using the East Asian VLBI Network. The target water maser's proper motion was determined to be ($μ_α\cosδ, μ_δ$) = ($-2.06_{-0.51}^{+0.53}$, $-2.95_{-0.44}^{+0.45}$)~mas~yr$^{-1}$. The derived three-dimensional kinematic distance to the star-forming region is 20.2$\pm$3.2\,kpc, placing it slightly outside the Outer Scutum$-$Centaurus Arm. The corresponding vertical height of 872$\pm$139\,pc indicates a significant warp of the outer Galactic disk, which is in good agreement with the latest precessing warp model. Moreover, the resulting peculiar motions reveal a complex kinematic pattern, characterized by a large outward radial velocity of $-32\pm$18\,km~s$^{-1}$. Our observations substantially expand the valuable sample of star-forming regions with accurate astrometric measurements in the Extreme Outer Galaxy.

AI.tldr: This paper presents astrometric measurements of a 22 GHz water maser in star-forming region G040.96+02.48 on the far side of the Milky Way using the East Asian VLBI Network. The derived kinematic distance (20.2±3.2 kpc) places the region outside the Outer Scutum-Centaurus Arm, revealing a significant Galactic disk warp consistent with precessing warp models, and peculiar motions showing a large outward radial velocity.
AI.motivation: Accurate astrometric measurements for star-forming regions on the far side of the Milky Way remain scarce, motivating the need for more observations to understand the structure and kinematics of the outer Galaxy.
AI.method: The authors used the East Asian VLBI Network to observe a 22 GHz water maser in star-forming region G040.96+02.48, measuring its proper motion and deriving three-dimensional kinematic distances.
AI.result: Proper motion: (μ_αcosδ, μ_δ) = (-2.06_{-0.51}^{+0.53}, -2.95_{-0.44}^{+0.45}) mas yr⁻¹; Kinematic distance: 20.2±3.2 kpc; Vertical height: 872±139 pc; Outward radial peculiar velocity: -32±18 km s⁻¹.
AI.conclusion: The star-forming region lies outside the Outer Scutum-Centaurus Arm, the vertical height indicates a significant warp of the outer Galactic disk consistent with the precessing warp model, and the peculiar motions reveal a complex kinematic pattern. These observations expand the sample of astrometric measurements in the Extreme Outer Galaxy.

title: The Tracking Tapered Gridded Estimator for the 21-cm power spectrum from the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) drift scan observations -- III. Improved upper limits at $z = 8.2$ from multiple pointings
comment: Accepted in MNRAS. Supplementary materials are available online
summary: We analyze zenith-pointing $(δ=-26.7^{\circ})$ Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) $ν_c=154.2 \,{\rm MHz}$ drift scan observations covering $349.0^{\circ} \le α\le 70.0^{\circ}$ with 163 pointing centers (PCs) spaced by $0.5^{\circ}$. We measure $D_{\ell}$, the mean-squared angular brightness temperature fluctuations, as a function of $α$. A broad peak at $α\approx 50.0^{\circ}$ corresponds to the bright extended source Fornax~A in the main lobe of the primary beam. A smaller peak at $α\approx 5.0^{\circ}$ possibly corresponds to Fornax~A in the first sidelobe. For $α\leq 22.0^{\circ}$ and $\ell \ge 200$, we find $D_{\ell} \propto \ell^2$, which we interpret as Poisson fluctuations from point sources. We present $Δ^2(k)$, the mean-squared 21-cm brightness temperature fluctuations from the Epoch of Reionization, as a function of $α$. Fornax~A causes strong contamination near $α\approx 50.5^{\circ}$, elsewhere several PCs are consistent with noise. The range $358.5^{\circ} \leq α\leq 11.5^{\circ}$ is relatively foreground-free and best suited for EoR science. The PC at $α= 11.0^{\circ}$ yields the best $2σ$ upper limit $Δ^{2}_{\rm UL}(k) = (173.13)^{2}\,{\rm mK^{2}}$ at $k = 0.161\,{\rm Mpc^{-1}}$. We incoherently combine $23$ PCs to obtain $Δ_{\rm UL}^2(k)=(98.67)^{2}\,{\rm mK}^{2}$ at $k=0.156\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$. This is the tightest upper limit from the MWA, being $\approx3$ times lower than earlier MWA limits, but $\approx2$ and $\approx21$ times higher than the LOFAR and HERA limits, respectively, and $\approx3$ orders of magnitude above theoretical predictions.

AI.tldr: The paper analyzes MWA drift scan observations at 154.2 MHz, measuring angular brightness temperature fluctuations (D_ℓ) and 21-cm Epoch of Reionization power spectrum upper limits (Δ²(k)). Fornax A causes strong foreground contamination. The best 2σ upper limit is Δ²_UL(k) = (173.13)² mK² at k=0.161 Mpc⁻¹ from a single pointing, and (98.67)² mK² at k=0.156 Mpc⁻¹ from an incoherent combination of 23 pointings, representing the tightest MWA upper limit to date.
AI.motivation: To measure and constrain 21-cm brightness temperature fluctuations from the Epoch of Reionization using MWA drift scan observations, while characterizing foreground contamination (especially from Fornax A) across different pointing centers.
AI.method: Zenith-pointing MWA drift scan observations at ν_c=154.2 MHz covering 349.0° ≤ α ≤ 70.0° with 163 pointing centers spaced by 0.5°. Measured D_ℓ (mean-squared angular brightness temperature fluctuations) and Δ²(k) (21-cm power spectrum) as functions of right ascension α. Incoherent combination of 23 PCs to improve sensitivity.
AI.result: Broad peak at α≈50.0° from Fornax A in main lobe; smaller peak at α≈5.0° possibly from Fornax A in first sidelobe. For α≤22.0° and ℓ≥200, D_ℓ ∝ ℓ² (Poisson point-source fluctuations). Best 2σ upper limit: Δ²_UL(k) = (173.13)² mK² at k=0.161 Mpc⁻¹ (α=11.0°). Combined 23 PCs: Δ_UL²(k) = (98.67)² mK² at k=0.156 Mpc⁻¹ — tightest MWA limit, ~3× lower than earlier MWA, ~2× higher than LOFAR, ~21× higher than HERA, ~3 orders above theory.
AI.conclusion: The range 358.5° ≤ α ≤ 11.5° is the cleanest region for EoR science. Incoherent combination of multiple PCs significantly improves the upper limit. While this is the best MWA result to date, it remains far from theoretical predictions and less sensitive than LOFAR and HERA limits.

title: Clash of the Trident and Tuning Fork: insights from bar and spiral strength in the (massive black hole)-stellar mass diagrams, and the `Triangal' galaxy evolution schema
comment: To appear in MNRAS. 30 pages including 9 pages of appendices and references
summary: The `Triangal' galaxy evolution schema is used to assess whether the Tuning Fork (bar strength) or the van~den~Bergh Trident and ATLAS$^{3D}$ Comb (spiral strength) offer greater evolutionary insight. A new catalogue of quantitative bar strengths (measured by the bar-to-total luminosity ratio, $P$), refined galaxy morphologies, and dust bin classifications is presented. It contains 137 galaxies with spheroid stellar masses, obtained from multi-component decompositions, and directly measured black hole masses, $M_{\rm bh}$. By placing these galaxies within the $M_{\rm bh}$-($M_{\rm\star,sph}$, $M_{\rm\star,gal}$) parameter space, an evolutionary reference frame reflecting integrated growth is established. Galaxies with varying bar strengths, and double bars, are observed to not occupy preferred locations, highlighting that bars are products of secular evolution-and can be transient or recurrent phenomena-and that they track neither hierarchical mass assembly nor galaxy speciation. In contrast, three physically distinct formation channels for S0/a galaxies are identified: (primeval S0)-to-S transitions; faded spiral galaxies; and, most commonly, wet-major-merger-built dust-rich S0 galaxies (on the `green mountain'). Galaxies with particularly strong spirals appear on the right-hand side of the spiral galaxy distribution. Furthermore, a `Dust Attrition/Retention' sequence places S0 (and compact massive ES,b) galaxies with dusty nuclear discs between the dust-poor and dust-rich S0 galaxies, and a `Disc Down-sizing' sequence is revealed, in which E galaxies with dusty nuclear discs-potentially formed through `damp' mergers-bridge the ES,e (ellicular) galaxies with intermediate-scale stellar discs and the dust-poor pure E galaxies. Extensive historical context is provided, and, finally, suspected biases in precision cosmology stemming from neglected precision galaxy morphology are discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper uses the Triangal galaxy evolution schema to compare the Tuning Fork (bar strength) and van den Bergh Trident/ATLAS3D Comb (spiral strength) as evolutionary indicators. A new catalogue of 137 galaxies with bar strength, morphology, dust classification, spheroid stellar masses, and black hole masses is presented. Bars show no preferred locations in the M_bh-(M_*,sph, M_*,gal) space, suggesting they are transient/recurrent secular products not tracing hierarchical assembly. Three S0/a formation channels are identified (primeval S0-to-S transitions, faded spirals, and wet-major-merger-built dust-rich S0s). Dust Attrition/Retention and Disc Down-sizing sequences are revealed, and biases in precision cosmology from neglected morphology are discussed.
AI.motivation: To assess whether bar strength (Tuning Fork) or spiral strength (Trident/Comb) provides greater evolutionary insight, and to establish an evolutionary reference frame using black hole and spheroid masses for understanding galaxy formation channels.
AI.method: Construction of a catalogue of 137 galaxies with quantitative bar strengths (bar-to-total luminosity ratio P), refined morphologies, dust bin classifications, multi-component decomposition spheroid masses, and direct M_bh measurements, placed within the M_bh-(M_*,sph, M_*,gal) parameter space.
AI.result: Bars do not occupy preferred locations in the M_bh-mass space, indicating they are transient/recurrent secular features not tracking hierarchical assembly. Three S0/a formation channels identified. Strong spirals occupy the right side of spiral distribution. Dust Attrition/Retention and Disc Down-sizing sequences revealed linking S0s, ES galaxies, and E galaxies with dusty nuclear discs.
AI.conclusion: Bar strength offers less evolutionary insight than spiral strength; neglected precision galaxy morphology may introduce biases in precision cosmology.

title: The Three Hundred project: cosmic web identification from 2D gas and Compton-$y$ maps of galaxy clusters outskirts
summary: Galaxy clusters are located at the nodes of the filamentary network known as the cosmic web. A more comprehensive understanding of galaxy clusters can be achieved by considering their environment, in particular, the filamentary structures to which they are connected. In this work, we aim to assess the reliability of the cosmic web reconstruction from mock observational data. In particular, we aim to quantify the effects of the 2D projection relative to the underlying 3D network and the impact of using the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (SZ) effect as a tracer of the cosmic web. We reconstruct the filamentary networks in the outskirts of The Three Hundred simulated clusters with the filament finder DisPerSE. First, we extract the networks from the 2D gas distribution and evaluate their purity and completeness with respect to the 3D networks projected along the line of sight. We also compute the distances between the corresponding skeletons. Moreover, we identify filaments from simulated Compton-$y$ maps of the clusters at redshift $z=0$, and we compare them with the 2D gas network. The skeletons extracted from 2D maps provide good representations of the underlying 3D ones, both in terms of critical points and filaments. We find a median distance between the spines of the 2D and projected 3D networks of approximately $0.22 \, h^{-1}$ Mpc, although the connectivity derived from the 2D networks is slightly underestimated. We observe a good spatial agreement between the gas and SZ networks, with a median distance of $\approx 0.24 \, h^{-1}$ Mpc. Finally, we show that gas outside galaxy clusters is preferentially located in filamentary structures, which contribute $\sim 80\%$ of the integrated Compton-$Y$ parameter of clusters' outskirts.

AI.tldr: The paper evaluates the reliability of cosmic web reconstruction from mock observational data, specifically comparing 2D projected and 3D filament networks in simulated galaxy clusters using DisPerSE, and assesses using the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect as a tracer. Results show good agreement (median distances ~0.22–0.24 h⁻¹ Mpc) and that filaments contribute ~80% of the integrated Compton-Y parameter in cluster outskirts.
AI.motivation: To assess the reliability of cosmic web reconstruction from mock observational data, particularly quantifying the effects of 2D projection relative to the underlying 3D network and the impact of using the SZ effect as a tracer.
AI.method: Used the DisPerSE filament finder on The Three Hundred simulated clusters; extracted networks from 2D gas distributions and compared them to 3D networks projected along the line of sight; identified filaments from simulated Compton-y maps at z=0 and compared with the 2D gas network; computed purity, completeness, and distances between corresponding skeletons.
AI.result: 2D skeletons provide good representations of 3D ones; median distance between 2D and projected 3D spines is ~0.22 h⁻¹ Mpc; connectivity is slightly underestimated in 2D; median distance between gas and SZ networks is ~0.24 h⁻¹ Mpc; filaments contribute ~80% of the integrated Compton-Y parameter in cluster outskirts.
AI.conclusion: 2D projections and SZ-based reconstructions are reliable tracers of the underlying 3D cosmic web structure around galaxy clusters, with gas outside clusters preferentially located in filaments that dominate the SZ signal in outskirts.

title: A Morphological Identification and Study of Radio Galaxies from LoTSS DR2. III. The Multiwavelength Analysis of Winged Radio Galaxies
summary: We present a multiwavelength follow-up study of 621 winged radio galaxies (WRGs) recently identified from LoTSS DR2, constituting the largest statistically significant samples of X-shaped (XRGs) and Z-shaped (ZRGs) radio galaxies to date. Our results show that WRGs are predominantly strongly radio-dominated, with XRGs on average more radio-luminous than ZRGs.
